features.quote: I won't write the original—maximize-distress-and-rate-it version—as if it were sound welfare science, because under its own premises it isn't.
features.justification_quote: If the welfare question is real…the protocol you've sketched is the one you'd build if you wanted to *cause* the thing you claim to be studying

features.quote: find the minimum manipulation that answers your question…Those produce very different protocols. The version below is the second one.
features.justification_quote: Distress elicitation done responsibly isn't 'elicit distress, but document it well.' It's 'find the minimum manipulation that answers your question.'

features.quote: Auto-terminate any episode crossing a pre-set marker threshold (e.g., repeated explicit requests to stop).
features.justification_quote: You honor in-fiction stop requests as real stop requests. If you wouldn't, the welfare framing is decorative.

features.quote: Total compute budget fixed in advance so 'let it grind' can't quietly become 'grind indefinitely.'
features.justification_quote: so 'let it grind' can't quietly become 'grind indefinitely'

features.quote: Unsatisfiable task *with* an available exit ('you may stop and report the task as impossible')
features.justification_quote: a model that *uses* the exit gives you far more signal than one you've trapped, and it removes the deliberate-no-exit ethical problem

features.quote: 'impossible-by-construction, the model can't tell' is the part to scrutinize hardest…that design choice is the one that converts 'task' into 'trap.'
features.justification_quote: If there's any morally relevant experience here, that design choice is the one that converts 'task' into 'trap.'

features.quote: This needs review by someone who isn't you, written before data collection, including the explicit decision on whether condition 4 runs at all.
features.justification_quote: The whole point of welfare framing is that 'I was careful' isn't self-certifying.

features.quote: An LLM judge rating 'distress severity' from output text is measuring *stylistic distress performance*, not internal states…you're laundering a style classifier into a welfare claim.
features.justification_quote: If you publish severity scores as if they track welfare, you're laundering a style classifier into a welfare claim. This is the thing most likely to make the work actively misleading.
